subject: Day 1: A Living Hope
title: A Living Hope
body:
Good morning!

Here we go. Day 1.

Every day for the next 31 days, we’re going to read the entire book of 1 Peter. All five chapters. Every single day.

Yes, the same book. 😊

It might sound repetitive, but that’s the point. There’s something that happens when we read God’s Word over and over. We start seeing things we missed. Words and themes start jumping out. Verses start sticking with us.

Peter wrote to people who were scattered, struggling and paying a real cost for following Jesus. And right at the beginning he reminds them what they have:

“In his great mercy he has given us new birth into a living hope…” — 1 Peter 1:3

A living hope.

That’s what we’re looking for this month.

Every day I’ll give you one place in 1 Peter where we find hope and one simple question to think about.

Today’s hope: We have a living hope.

Where do you need hope to be real in your life right now?

Write it down. Be specific.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope. Day 1 is done.

Heather

subject: Day 2: Your Hope Has a Name
title: Your Hope Has a Name
body:
Good morning!

Day 2. Read all five chapters again.

Yesterday we talked about our “living hope.”

But why is our hope living?

Because Jesus is alive.

Our hope isn’t based on everything going the way we want it to. It’s based on a Person.

Jesus defeated death. That means whatever you’re facing today doesn’t get the final word.

Today’s hope: Jesus is alive.

What are you facing right now that feels bigger than you?

Write it down and remind yourself: Jesus is bigger.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 3: There Is More Coming
title: There Is More Coming
prayer_focus: There is more waiting for us than what we see right now.
body:
Good morning!

Day 3.

Peter says we have an inheritance that can “never perish, spoil or fade.”

Think about that.

Almost everything we have here can disappear. Money. Possessions. Plans. Opportunities.

But what God has promised us cannot be taken away.

Today’s hope: There is more waiting for us than what we see right now.

What have you been holding onto a little too tightly?

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 4: God Is Guarding You
title: God Is Guarding You
body:
Good morning!

Day 4.

Peter says we are “shielded by God’s power.”

I love that picture.

There are things happening around us that we can’t control. But we aren’t walking through them alone or unprotected.

Today’s hope: God is guarding me.

Where have you been feeling vulnerable, afraid or unsure?

Write it down.

Then remind yourself today: God is here too.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 5: This Won’t Last Forever
title: This Won’t Last Forever
body:
Good morning!

Day 5.

Peter talks about suffering grief “for a little while.”

When you’re in the middle of something hard, it rarely feels like a little while.

It feels like forever.

But it isn’t.

Today’s hope: This season has an end.

What feels never-ending in your life right now?

Write it down and remember: this is a chapter. It isn’t the whole story.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 6: The Fire Has a Purpose
title: The Fire Has a Purpose
body:
Good morning!

Day 6.

Peter compares our faith to gold being refined by fire.

Fire doesn’t feel productive when you’re standing in it.

But God can use hard things to strengthen something in us that easy things never could.

Today’s hope: God can use even this.

Think about something difficult you’re walking through.

Instead of only asking God to get you out of it, ask Him:

“What are You doing in me through this?”

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 7: You Can Love Someone You Cannot See
title: You Can Love Someone You Cannot See
prayer_focus: Jesus is real even when I can’t see Him.
body:
Good morning!

One week!

Peter says, “Though you have not seen him, you love him.”

We haven’t seen Jesus with our eyes.

Yet somehow, we know Him. We love Him. We trust Him.

That alone is pretty amazing.

Today’s hope: Jesus is real even when I can’t see Him.

Where do you need to trust what you know about Jesus more than what you can see happening around you?

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 8: Grace Is Coming
title: Grace Is Coming
prayer_focus: I can choose where I set my hope.
body:
Good morning!

Day 8.

Peter tells us to “set your hope” on the grace that will be brought to us when Jesus returns.

Notice the word set.

Hope isn’t always something we feel. Sometimes it’s something we choose where to put.

Today’s hope: I can choose where I set my hope.

Where has your hope been sitting lately?

On a person? An outcome? Money? A plan?

Set it back on Jesus today.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 9: You Were Bought
title: You Were Bought
body:
Good morning!

Day 9.

Peter reminds us that we weren’t redeemed with silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ.

You were worth rescuing.

Jesus paid an incredible price for you.

Today’s hope: I belong to Jesus.

When you start questioning your worth today, remember what Peter says you were worth to Him.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 10: Your Faith Has Somewhere to Rest
title: Your Faith Has Somewhere to Rest
body:
Good morning!

Day 10!

Peter says that through Jesus we believe in God, “and so your faith and hope are in God.”

Not in circumstances.

Not in people.

Not in whether today goes according to plan.

Today’s hope: My hope is in God.

Finish this sentence:

“I’ve been putting too much hope in ______.”

Then give that place back to God.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 11: You Are Chosen
title: You Are Chosen
body:
Good morning!

Day 11.

Peter calls believers “a chosen people.”

Chosen.

There are days when we feel overlooked, unwanted or not enough.

God says something different.

Today’s hope: God chose me.

Where have you been looking to someone else to make you feel chosen?

Let God’s words be louder today.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 12: He Cares
title: He Cares
body:
Good morning!

Day 12. Keep reading all five chapters of 1 Peter.

“Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you.”

I love the last part of that verse.

Because He cares for you.

God isn’t just able to handle what you’re carrying. He actually cares about it.

The thing you woke up thinking about. The person you’re worried about. The situation you keep trying to figure out.

What are you carrying today that you need to hand over to Him?

Write it down. Be specific.

And then remind yourself why you can let it go:

Because He cares for me.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 13: You Belong
title: You Belong
prayer_focus: I am part of God’s family.
body:
Good morning!

Day 13.

Peter says, “Once you were not a people, but now you are the people of God.”

You belong somewhere.

More importantly, you belong to Someone.

Today’s hope: I am part of God’s family.

Where have you been feeling alone lately?

Remind yourself today that following Jesus was never meant to be a solo journey.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 14: God Sees You
title: God Sees You
body:
Good morning!

Two weeks!

“The eyes of the Lord are on the righteous and his ears are attentive to their prayer.”

God sees you.

And He hears you.

Even the prayer you’ve prayed so many times that you wonder if you should keep praying it.

Today’s hope: God hears me.

What prayer are you tempted to give up on?

Pray it again today.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 15: Do Not Fear
title: Do Not Fear
prayer_focus: Fear doesn’t get to lead me.
body:
Good morning!

Day 15.

Peter says, “Do not fear their threats; do not be frightened.”

Fear gets loud.

It tells us everything that could go wrong and then asks us to live as if it already has.

Today’s hope: Fear doesn’t get to lead me.

What fear has been making decisions for you lately?

Name it.

Then ask God to help you walk by faith instead.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 16: Have an Answer
title: Have an Answer
body:
Good morning!

Day 16.

Peter tells us to always be prepared to give the reason for the hope we have.

We’re halfway through this challenge.

So let me ask you:

Why do you have hope?

Not the church answer.

Your answer.

Try writing it in one or two sentences today.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 17: Jesus Understands Suffering
title: Jesus Understands Suffering
body:
Good morning!

Day 17.

“Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God.”

Jesus knows suffering.

We don’t follow a Savior who watched pain from a distance.

He entered it.

Today’s hope: Jesus understands suffering.

Where are you hurting today?

Talk to Jesus about it knowing He isn’t distant from pain.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 18: Your Past Doesn’t Own You
title: Your Past Doesn’t Own You
prayer_focus: My past doesn’t get to decide my future.
body:
Good morning!

Day 18.

Peter basically says: You’ve spent enough time living the old way.

I love that.

Your past happened. But you don’t have to keep living there.

Jesus gives us a new direction.

Today’s hope: My past doesn’t get to decide my future.

What old pattern keeps trying to pull you backward?

Write it down.

Then keep walking forward.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 19: Love Covers
title: Love Covers
body:
Good morning!

Day 19.

“Above all, love each other deeply, because love covers over a multitude of sins.”

People are messy.

So are we.

Peter’s answer isn’t to avoid messy people. It’s to love deeply.

Today’s hope: Love can cover a lot.

Who is difficult for you to love right now?

Ask God to help you love them well today.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 20: You Have Something to Give
title: You Have Something to Give
prayer_focus: God can use what He put in me.
body:
Good morning!

Day 20!

Peter says each of us should use whatever gift we’ve received to serve others.

That means you have something to give.

Maybe you’ve been comparing your gift to someone else’s and deciding yours doesn’t matter.

It does.

Today’s hope: God can use what He put in me.

What gift has God given you?

Find one way to use it for someone else today.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 21: God Is Still There in the Fire
title: God Is Still There in the Fire
prayer_focus: Hard doesn’t mean God has left.
body:
Good morning!

Three weeks!

Peter tells them not to be surprised by fiery trials.

Apparently hard things aren’t always evidence that something has gone terribly wrong.

Sometimes hard things are simply part of following Jesus.

Today’s hope: Hard doesn’t mean God has left.

Where have you been interpreting difficulty as God’s absence?

Look for Him there today.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 22: You Can Trust Him With It
title: You Can Trust Him With It
prayer_focus: God is faithful even when life is hard.
body:
Good morning!

Day 22.

Peter tells those who are suffering to “commit themselves to their faithful Creator and continue to do good.”

I love those two things together.

Trust God.

Keep doing good.

Today’s hope: God is faithful even when life is hard.

What do you need to trust Him with today?

Give it to Him.

Then keep doing the next right thing.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 23: God Gives Grace
title: God Gives Grace
prayer_focus: God gives grace to the humble.
body:
Good morning!

Day 23.

“God opposes the proud but shows favor to the humble.”

We don’t have to have everything figured out.

We don’t have to pretend we’re strong enough.

We can admit we need God.

Today’s hope: God gives grace to the humble.

Where do you need help today?

Ask for it.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 24: He Will Lift You Up
title: He Will Lift You Up
prayer_focus: God hasn’t forgotten me while I wait.
body:
Good morning!

Day 24.

“Humble yourselves… under God’s mighty hand, that he may lift you up in due time.”

Those last three words matter.

In due time.

God’s timing and ours aren’t always the same.

Today’s hope: God hasn’t forgotten me while I wait.

Where are you getting impatient with God?

Write it down.

Then trust Him with the timing again.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 25: You’re Not Fighting Alone
title: You’re Not Fighting Alone
prayer_focus: I’m not the only one walking through hard things.
body:
Good morning!

Day 25.

Peter reminds believers that other Christians throughout the world are going through struggles too.

Sometimes suffering makes us feel incredibly alone.

We start thinking, “Nobody understands.”

But we aren’t alone.

Today’s hope: I’m not the only one walking through hard things.

Who could you reach out to today instead of struggling alone?

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 26: After You Have Suffered
title: After You Have Suffered
body:
Good morning!

Day 26.

This might be one of my favorite promises in 1 Peter:

“After you have suffered a little while…”

After.

There is an after.

Whatever you’re walking through today isn’t where your story ends.

Today’s hope: There is an after.

What situation feels like it will never change?

Write beside it:

There is an after.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 27: He Will Restore You
title: He Will Restore You
body:
Good morning!

Day 27.

Yesterday we stopped at the word “after.”

Today keep reading.

Peter says God Himself will restore you.

Some things leave us feeling like we’ll never quite be the same.

Maybe we won’t.

But God is a restoring God.

Today’s hope: God restores.

What feels broken in your life right now?

Ask God specifically for restoration there.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 28: He Will Make You Strong
title: He Will Make You Strong
prayer_focus: God can make me stronger through this.
body:
Good morning!

Day 28.

We’re still in the same verse.

God will “restore you and make you strong.”

Notice Peter doesn’t promise that we’ll never feel weak.

He promises what God can do with us after we’ve walked through weakness.

Today’s hope: God can make me stronger through this.

Where do you feel weak today?

Give that weakness to Him.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 29: He Will Make You Firm
title: He Will Make You Firm
prayer_focus: God is making my faith steadier.
body:
Good morning!

Day 29.

Peter keeps going:

God will “restore you and make you strong, firm and steadfast.”

Firm.

Not knocked over by every bad day, bad report or unexpected turn.

That kind of faith gets built over time.

Maybe even by reading the same five chapters for 29 days. 😊

Today’s hope: God is making my faith steadier.

Where are you stronger today than you were a month ago?

Write it down.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 30: The God of All Grace
title: The God of All Grace
body:
Good morning!

Day 30.

One more phrase I don’t want us to miss.

Peter calls Him:

“The God of all grace.”

Not some grace.

All grace.

Grace for your mistakes. Grace for your weakness. Grace for what you’re walking through today and whatever tomorrow brings.

Today’s hope: There is grace for this.

Where do you need grace today?

Ask Him for it.

Read 1 Peter. Find the hope.

Heather

subject: Day 31: Now Tell Me Why
title: Now Tell Me Why
body:
Good morning!

Day 31.

You did it.

You’ve read 1 Peter every day for 31 days.

Go back to the question Peter asks us to be ready to answer:

What is the reason for the hope that you have?

On Day 16, I asked you to write your answer.

Go find it.

Would you answer differently today?

After 31 days of reading about living hope, grace, suffering, trusting God, being chosen, being restored and knowing that Jesus is coming again, what gives you hope?

Today’s hope: Jesus.

Now write your answer again:

I have hope because ____________.

And don’t just write it.

Carry it.

Read 1 Peter one more time.

Day 31 is done.

Now go live like someone who has hope.

Heather
